source.citation: J. Chao, B. J. Zwolinski, Ideal gas thermodynamic properties of methanoic and ethanoic acids, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 7 (1978) 363-377
source.access: Free NIST reprint of J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data (NIST Standard Reference Data)
source.tables: Table 8 (equilibrium constants K_eq, 1/atm), p. 369; Table 5 (reported enthalpies of dimerization), p. 368

basis: The constants come from the authors' statistical-thermodynamic tables for monomer and dimer, with the enthalpy of dimerization (-15.25 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, uncertainty 0.15 kcal/mol, p. 374) chosen so that they reproduce the measured vapour densities of Coolidge (1928). Table 5 lists the measured values: P-V-T (vapour density) by Coolidge 1928 (283-429 K), Halford 1942, Taylor and Bruton 1952 (323-423 K) and Barton and Hsu 1969, and spectroscopic values.
check: Each K_eq agrees with the table's own dimer mole fractions at 1 atm, y_D / (1 - y_D)^2 (for example 400 K: 0.276 / 0.724^2 = 0.527 against 0.525).
notes: Transcribed from the page image of Table 8; the rows at 100, 200, 700 and 800 K (6.33e24, 1.15e8, 1.68e-4, 4.51e-5) are outside the range fitted. The person compares each value with the table.
